questions.question: Where was Guru Gobind Singh Ji born in 1666?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh Ji was born at Patna in Bihar in 1666 while his father was travelling in the east.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: What was Guru Gobind Singh Ji's name before the creation of the Khalsa?
questions.explanation: He was born Gobind Rai and took the name Gobind Singh when he received Amrit from the Panj Pyare in 1699.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: Who was the mother of Guru Gobind Singh Ji?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh Ji's mother was Mata Gujari Ji, wife of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: Paonta Sahib, where Guru Gobind Singh Ji lived and wrote much poetry, lies on the bank of which river?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh Ji founded Paonta on the Yamuna, where much of his literary work was done.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: In the Battle of Bhangani (1688), Guru Gobind Singh Ji defeated hill rulers led by which raja?
options: Raja Fateh Chand (Fateh Shah) of Garhwal
questions.explanation: At Bhangani, near Paonta, the Guru defeated the hill chiefs led by Raja Fateh Chand of Garhwal.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: In which year did Guru Gobind Singh Ji create the Khalsa on Vaisakhi?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh Ji created the Khalsa on Vaisakhi in 1699.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: Who was the father of Guru Gobind Singh Ji?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh Ji was the son of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, the ninth Guru, who was travelling in Bengal and Assam at the time of his birth in Patna.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism – Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: Which of these was one of the Panj Pyare?
questions.explanation: The Panj Pyare were Bhai Daya Singh, Bhai Dharam Singh, Bhai Himmat Singh, Bhai Mohkam Singh and Bhai Sahib Singh.
questions.source: SikhNet: Panj Piare

questions.question: Bhai Daya Singh, one of the Panj Pyare, came from which city?
questions.explanation: Bhai Daya Singh (formerly Daya Ram) was a Khatri from Lahore.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: With what was the Amrit stirred at the first Khalsa initiation in 1699?
questions.explanation: Khande di pahul was prepared by stirring sweetened water with a double-edged Khanda while Gurbani was recited.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: After initiating the Panj Pyare, what did Guru Gobind Singh Ji do?
options: He went to Delhi to meet the emperor
He asked the Panj Pyare to initiate him with Amrit
He appointed one of them as the next Guru
questions.explanation: The Guru received Amrit from the Panj Pyare himself, becoming Gobind Singh, showing the Khalsa's equality with the Guru.
questions.source: SikhNet: Panj Piare

questions.question: Which two Sahibzade attained martyrdom fighting at the Battle of Chamkaur in December 1705?
options: Baba Zorawar Singh and Baba Fateh Singh
Baba Ajit Singh and Baba Zorawar Singh
Baba Jujhar Singh and Baba Fateh Singh
Baba Ajit Singh and Baba Jujhar Singh
questions.explanation: The elder Sahibzade, Baba Ajit Singh and Baba Jujhar Singh, fell fighting at Chamkaur on 7 December 1705.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: To which emperor did Guru Gobind Singh Ji address the Zafarnama?
questions.explanation: The Zafarnama ('Epistle of Victory') was addressed to Emperor Aurangzeb.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: In which language did Guru Gobind Singh Ji write the Zafarnama?
questions.explanation: The Zafarnama is written in Persian verse.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: Jaap Sahib, recited in the morning Nitnem and during Amrit preparation, appears at the beginning of which scripture?
questions.explanation: Jaap Sahib by Guru Gobind Singh Ji opens the Dasam Granth and is one of the five morning Nitnem banis.
questions.source: SikhNet: Jaap Sahib

questions.question: At Damdama Sahib (Talwandi Sabo), Guru Gobind Singh Ji prepared the final recension of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. Who served as the scribe?
questions.explanation: Bhai Mani Singh Ji wrote out the recension at Damdama Sahib, which included the bani of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: Where did Guru Gobind Singh Ji pass away in 1708?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh Ji passed away at Nanded in present-day Maharashtra in October 1708.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: Before his passing in 1708, to whom did Guru Gobind Singh Ji pass the eternal Guruship?
questions.explanation: He declared Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji the eternal Guru, ending the line of personal Gurus.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: What was Banda Singh Bahadur's name before he met Guru Gobind Singh Ji at Nanded?
questions.explanation: The Bairagi ascetic Madho Das met the Guru at Nanded, was initiated and became known as Banda Singh.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru

questions.question: When sending Banda Singh Bahadur to Punjab, what did Guru Gobind Singh Ji give him as a token of authority?
questions.explanation: The Guru gave Banda Singh five arrows and an escort of five Sikhs, and sent him to fight tyranny in Punjab.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University): Gobind Singh, Guru
